decided: What the brief says about whether a change's requirements were synced, and about the archive's own warnings, follows only what the archive's run record for the change says: the sync ran, the sync was skipped, or the change was archived with no record at all. A change not yet archived says no archive has recorded a sync yet. The list of records no reader checked is taken when the brief is made, so the copy saved at archive says that records written after it appear in the archived change's brief and the program brief.
alternatives: decide the label only by whether an archive record exists, which told old archived changes their requirements were not yet synced
work out the real state by comparing each requirement to the project's current specs
why: Each line is then true by construction, including for changes archived before orbit kept archive records and for an archive that skipped the sync; comparing against the current specs would mislead once a later change edits the same requirement. The user chose this at the proposal review.
